data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: Records Management
extract_result.opi: br/>Office of the Chief Information Officer – Information Resources Management
extract_result.purpose: This regulation sets out and summarizes the policies, responsibilities for the creation, maintenance, use, and disposition of all records and other documentary materials throughout the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) in compliance with the Federal Records Act (FRA) as codified at 44 United States Code (U.S.C.) Chapters 29, 31, and 33; Subchapter B, Records Management, 36 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR); and all applicable National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) mandated guidance. It also sets out role and responsibilities of personnel in various USDA positions with respect to records.
extract_result.scope: This directive applies to all USDA agencies, staff offices, employees, and contractors working for or on behalf of USDA and all USDA records, regardless of medium, which are created, collected, processed, used, stored, and/or destroyed by USDA agencies. Each USDA agency and staff office is obligated to meet the minimum requirements of this policy. Agencies are required to integrate records management into the overall information resources management program, in accordance with 36 CFR Subchapter B, Records Management, and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-130 (Revised), Management of Federal Information Resources.

Chapters 29, 31, and 33; Subchapter B, Records Management, 36 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR); and all applicable National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) mandated guidance.

Agencies are required to integrate records management into the overall information resources management program, in accordance with 36 CFR Subchapter B, Records Management, and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-130 (Revised), Management of Federal Information Resources.

policy_statements.source_text: This directive supersedes Departmental Regulation (DR) 3080-001, dated May 23, 2013, in its entirety, is effective immediately and will remain in effect until superseded or overtaken by a subsequent DR or government-wide guidance.
conditions: until superseded or overtaken by a subsequent DR or government-wide guidance

policy_statements.source_text: It is USDA policy to preserve all official records, in accordance with applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, and to promote access to information by staff and the public, as appropriate.
Each agency and staff office within USDA is required to establish and maintain a records management program meeting the following minimum requirements:

Accurately and completely create and preserve records, in any medium (including social media), containing documentation of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, and essential transactions of the agency or staff office that protects the legal and financial rights of the Government and persons directly affected by agency or staff activities as required by the FRA;
policy_statements.actor_name: agency and staff office within USDA
policy_statements.target: records, in any medium (including social media)

policy_statements.source_text: Establish records management standards and procedures for maintaining USDA records and information in a manner facilitating ease of use, access and disposition, and consistent with the regulations and guidelines implemented by NARA, the OMB, and the General Services Administration (GSA);
policy_statements.actor_name: agency and staff office within USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Establish effective management controls over the creation, maintenance and use, and disposition of Federal records in any medium, including but not limited to: paper, e-mail, instant messaging (IM), text messages, telephone messages, voice mail messages, presentations, Web sites, social media, word processing documents, spreadsheets, and information systems, throughout their life cycle;
policy_statements.actor_name: agency and staff office within USDA
policy_statements.target: creation, maintenance and use, and disposition of Federal records in any medium

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure records in any medium, are accessible to departmental officials and to the public as appropriate;
policy_statements.actor_name: agency and staff office within USDA
conditions: as appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the laws, regulations, and policies that apply to records and information used and maintained by USDA also apply to USDA records and information maintained and used on USDA’s behalf by USDA contractors.
policy_statements.actor_name: agency and staff office within USDA
policy_statements.target: laws, regulations, and policies that apply to records and information used and maintained by USDA

policy_statements.source_text: All records created by USDA contractors shall remain the property of USDA, and cannot be used except as explicitly authorized in writing by USDA (see Appendix A and B);
policy_statements.target: All records created by USDA contractors
conditions: except as explicitly authorized in writing by USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Establish procedures to ensure Federal records that are created by use of personal or non-official electronic messaging accounts for official USDA business are preserved for FRA purposes and placed in a record keeping system (see Appendix C);
policy_statements.actor_name: agency and staff office within USDA
conditions: that are created by use of personal or non-official electronic messaging accounts for official USDA business

policy_statements.source_text: Establish procedures to ensure Federal records created by use of text messaging, IM or other transient messaging technologies are preserved for FRA purposes and placed in a record keeping system (see Appendix C); and
policy_statements.actor_name: agency and staff office within USDA
conditions: created by use of text messaging, IM or other transient messaging technologies

policy_statements.source_text: Establish and maintain a vital records program to ensure continuity of essential USDA activities during and following a national emergency or local natural or technological disaster (see also DR 3085-001, Vital Records Management Program).
policy_statements.actor_name: agency and staff office within USDA

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Secretary shall:

Make and preserve records containing adequate and proper documentation of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, and essential transactions of the Department by establishing a records management program to ensure compliance with applicable Federal laws and guidelines;
policy_statements.target: records containing adequate and proper documentation of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, and essential transactions of the Department

policy_statements.source_text: Designate a Senior Agency Official (SAO), at the Assistant Secretary level or its equivalent, who has direct responsibility for ensuring USDA efficiently and appropriately complies with all applicable records management statutes, regulations, NARA policies, and requirements of the OMB/NARA M-12-18, Managing Government Records Directive.
cross_references: OMB/NARA M-12-18, Managing Government Records Directive

policy_statements.source_text: The Secretary has designated the Assistant Secretary for Administration as the SAO for records management.
Under Secretaries, Agency, and Staff Office Heads shall:
Provide adequate staff resources to support records management processes within their respective organizations;
policy_statements.actor_name: Under Secretaries, Agency, and Staff Office Heads

policy_statements.source_text: Participate in developing new or revised programs, processes, systems, and procedures to ensure adequate record keeping processes are established and implemented within their respective organizations;
policy_statements.actor_name: Under Secretaries, Agency, and Staff Office Heads
policy_statements.target: new or revised programs, processes, systems, and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: Provide records management briefings for all managers and records management training to all staff within their organizations;
policy_statements.actor_name: Under Secretaries, Agency, and Staff Office Heads
policy_statements.target: records management briefings for all managers and records management training to all staff within their organizations

policy_statements.source_text: Annually review the organization's record keeping practices in order to validate their accuracy and to ensure implementation;
policy_statements.actor_name: Under Secretaries, Agency, and Staff Office Heads

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure Information Technology (IT) managers coordinate with appropriate records management professionals to address records management requirements as identified in this directive;
policy_statements.actor_name: Under Secretaries, Agency, and Staff Office Heads

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the records staff is fully involved in all projects concerning the creation, maintenance, use, and disposition of all USDA records;
policy_statements.actor_name: Under Secretaries, Agency, and Staff Office Heads

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure organizations generating statements of work for USDA contracts involving creation or maintenance of Federal records include in the contracts appropriate records management requirements to comply with this directive and its authorities (see Appendix A and B); and
policy_statements.actor_name: Under Secretaries, Agency, and Staff Office Heads
policy_statements.target: organizations generating statements of work for USDA contracts involving creation or maintenance of Federal records

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure all records and other types of required documentary materials are not unlawfully removed from USDA by current or departing officials, employees, or contractors (see DR 3099-001, Records Management Policy for Departing Employees, Contractors, Volunteers and Political Appointees).
policy_statements.actor_name: Under Secretaries, Agency, and Staff Office Heads
cross_references: DR 3099-001, Records Management Policy for Departing Employees, Contractors, Volunteers and Political Appointees
policy_statements.target: all records and other types of required documentary materials

policy_statements.source_text: USDA SAO shall:
Ensure the Department efficiently and appropriately complies with all applicable records management statutes, regulations, NARA policies, and requirements of the OMB/NARA M-12-18;

Designate records officers (RO) within each USDA agency and staff office to develop and maintain a comprehensive records management program consistent with all established Departmental records management guidelines, and notify the departmental records officer of the assignment;
policy_statements.target: each USDA agency and staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure agency and staff office officials receive guidance on their programmatic and individual records management responsibilities and requirements; and
Submit the USDA’s annual records management report to the U.S. Government’s Chief Records Officer.
USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) shall:

Review proposed Department reporting and record keeping requirements, including those contained in rules and regulations, to ensure they impose the minimum burden upon the public and have practical utility for the Department (see Government Paperwork Elimination Act (GPEA) and DR 3410-001, Information Collection Activities-Collection of Information from the Public);
policy_statements.target: proposed Department reporting and record keeping requirements
cross_references: DR 3410-001, Information Collection Activities-Collection of Information from the Public

policy_statements.source_text: Administer the Departmental Records Management Program in compliance with NARA and other oversight agencies;
Address records management provisions in Capital Planning and Investment Control (CPIC) proposals and Enterprise Architecture (EA) plans:
policy_statements.target: records management provisions in Capital Planning and Investment Control (CPIC) proposals and Enterprise Architecture (EA) plans

policy_statements.source_text: In compliance with Records Management and OMB A-130 Circular, ensure records management and records archival functions are addressed in the requirements development phase for the design, development, and implementation of new or significantly revised information systems; and
policy_statements.target: records management and records archival functions

policy_statements.source_text: Integrate planning for electronic records management systems into plans for resource allocation and use, including budgeting, acquisition, and use of IT. (see NARA, Criteria for Managing Email Records in Compliance with the Managing Government Records Directive M-12-18).
cross_references: NARA, Criteria for Managing Email Records in Compliance with the Managing Government Records Directive M-12-18
policy_statements.target: planning for electronic records management systems

policy_statements.source_text: Departmental Records Officer (DRO) shall:
Develop Departmentwide policies, standards, and procedures for records management and provide oversight in their implementation;
policy_statements.target: Departmentwide policies, standards, and procedures for records management

policy_statements.source_text: Establish and maintain a list of USDA employees who are designated as agency or staff office RO;
policy_statements.target: list of USDA employees who are designated as agency or staff office RO

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the USDA representative to NARA, other Federal agencies, and external organizations on matters pertaining to the USDA’s records management program.
policy_statements.target: NARA, other Federal agencies, and external organizations

policy_statements.source_text: Collaborate with NARA and other regulatory agencies such as OMB and GSA in applying standards, procedures, and techniques to improve the management of records and promote the maintenance of those records of continuing value;
policy_statements.target: NARA and other regulatory agencies such as OMB and GSA

policy_statements.source_text: Develop and implement management systems and procedures to ensure officials, employees, contractors, volunteers, and interns do not remove Federal records from Department custody without appropriate authorization (see DR 3099-001, Records Management Policy for Departing Employees, Contractors, Volunteers and Political Appointees);
conditions: without appropriate authorization
cross_references: DR 3099-001, Records Management Policy for Departing Employees, Contractors, Volunteers and Political Appointees

policy_statements.source_text: Establish procedures for the participation of agency and staff office ROs in developing new or revised agency and staff office programs, processes, systems, and procedures to ensure adequate record keeping requirements are established and implemented;
policy_statements.target: procedures for the participation of agency and staff office ROs

policy_statements.source_text: Conduct reviews of agency and staff office ROs to evaluate program effectiveness and ensure conformance with Governmentwide and Departmentwide records management standards;
Conduct periodic evaluations of records management programs within USDA, as part of the records management and oversight program;
Review and approve costs for the storage of Federal records including the invoices for records stored in the Federal Records Centers (FRC); and
policy_statements.target: costs for the storage of Federal records

policy_statements.source_text: Establish a Departmentwide vital records program in compliance with NARA requirements (see DR 3085-001).
Agency and Staff Office ROs shall:
Assist the DRO in administering the records management program to ensure uniformity throughout the Department;
Provide the DRO with information and documentation requested for review of the agency or staff office records management program.
If requested, serve on the review team conducting an evaluation of the records management program of another agency or staff office;
conditions: If requested

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure their agency and staff office officials and employees receive guidance on their records management responsibilities and established record keeping requirements, by providing mandatory records management training appropriate for their records responsibilities;
policy_statements.target: their agency and staff office officials and employees

policy_statements.source_text: Develop and maintain current records disposition schedules for all agency or staff office records.
policy_statements.target: current records disposition schedules for all agency or staff office records

policy_statements.source_text: Review schedules, when notified of program changes resulting in:
conditions: when notified of program changes resulting in:

policy_statements.source_text: Establishing new types of records;
An increase or decrease in the retention time of the records; or
New or revised electronic systems.

Ensure permanent records are preserved and transferred to NARA and temporary records are transferred into off-site storage or destroyed promptly, according to NARA-approved records disposition schedules, unless subject to litigation hold or other preservation requirements;
conditions: unless subject to litigation hold or other preservation requirements

policy_statements.source_text: Conduct records management exit briefings, or establish protocols and procedures to ensure records management personnel conduct exit briefings, for employees and Presidential Appointees (see DR 3099-001);
Report any unlawful or accidental removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of Department records to the DRO and to NARA;
policy_statements.target: any unlawful or accidental removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of Department records

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with appropriate contracting officials to ensure necessary requirements are identified in contracts and deliverables, including:
Identify Federal records as contract deliverables or records for final turnover and other records specified as appropriate to the contract scope;
conditions: as appropriate to the contract scope

policy_statements.source_text: Distinguishing between Federal records and contractor-owned records;
Managing Federal records, in accordance with this directive and all other relevant laws, regulations, and USDA directives; and
Delivering records at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the contract, or at the termination of the contract (see Appendix A and B).

in accordance with the contract
at the termination of the contract

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the identification, maintenance, and protection of their agency’s and staff office’s vital records meet NARA requirements (see DR 3085-001).
policy_statements.target: identification, maintenance, and protection of their agency’s and staff office’s vital records

policy_statements.source_text: Program Managers shall:
Assign an official Records Management Liaison (RML) for each section within their operations.
This custodian is responsible for records management compliance within that section.
policy_statements.target: records management compliance within that section

policy_statements.source_text: For each program or office at least one records custodian is required to provide day-to-day administration of an organization’s records management program and, as appropriate, to act as liaison with the agency or staff office RO.
policy_statements.resulting_status: liaison with the agency or staff office RO
conditions: For each program or office
as appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: Provide names and contact information, and updates as changes occur, to the agency or staff office RO;
policy_statements.target: names and contact information, and updates as changes occur

policy_statements.source_text: Create those records needed to ensure adequate and proper documentation of their area of responsibility.
